QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r19.claim: A person is not left neglected and without moral responsibility.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r2.claim: The gathering-bones question is tightly connected to the ending's question whether humanity will be left neglected.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r2.anchor: أنها مرتبطةٌ بما ورد في آخر السورة وهو قوله: {أَيَحْسَبُ الإنسان أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r3.claim: The question whether humanity is left neglected links back to the oath, gathering bones, the record of deeds, the preceding threat, and the closing proof of God's power to resurrect.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r3.anchor: هذه الآية مرتبطة بأول السورة، وهو القَسم بيوم القيامة، ومرتبطة بقوله تعالى: {أَيَحْسَبُ الإنسان أَلَّن نَّجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ}

NAHHAS:v5p92/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r14.claim: The expression is also in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r14.anchor: في موضع نصب أيضا على الحال وروى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس أن معنى أن يترك سدى

NAHHAS:v5p92/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p92/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that being left suda means being left neglected.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r15.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس أن معنى أن يترك سدى يقول مهملا

SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r1.claim: Sudā is a circumstantial accusative from the subject of يُترك, meaning left unattended or neglected, like camels left untended.
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r1.anchor: حال من فاعل " يترك " ومعناه: مهملا يقال: إبل سدى، أي: مهملة.

SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r2.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses سدى for something created in vain or left without purpose: ‘God created nothing neglected.’
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r2.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
4427 وأقسم بالله جهد اليمين
ما خلق الله شيئا سدى

SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r3.claim: أسديت حاجتي means I neglected or wasted my need; أسدى إليه معروفا means he made a favor seem forgotten to its recipient, without recalling it or holding it over them.
SAMIN-DURR:75:36/r3.anchor: ومعنى " أسدى إليه معروفا " ، أي: جعله بمنزلة الضائع عند المسدى إليه

ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n15/r1.claim: To be left without purpose means not being held morally responsible for one's actions.
ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n15/r1.anchor: I.e., without being held morally responsible for his doings.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.claim: The agent is omitted from left aimless, created, fashioned, and made, matching the preceding passive and the sūra’s urgent tone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.anchor: وعدم ذكر فاعل الخلق وما بعده مناسب لحذف فاعل الترك. وكل ذلك مناسب لجو العجلة في السورة

QIRAAT-ER:75:36:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:75:36:1#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:75:36:1#1/r1.claim: The vw vowel reading shifts the imperfect stem from a to i while preserving ḥ-s-b semantics, marking a live recitation pattern.
QIRAAT-ER:75:36:1#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel reading shifts the imperfect stem vowel from a to i, preserving ḥ-s-b semantics

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#7/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#7/r1.claim: Qatāda explains being left suda as being neglected or abandoned without care.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#7/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أن يترك سدى ﴾ قال أن يهمل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r1.claim: Suda means left neglected: neither charged with duties nor recompensed; alternatively, left in the grave without resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r1.anchor: أي مهملا فلا يكلف ولا يجزى وقيل أن يترك في قبره فلا يبعث

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r2.claim: The word is used of camels grazing unattended; asdaytu can mean neglecting something, including a need one fails to pursue.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r2.anchor: ويقال إبل سدى أي مهملة ترعى حيث شاءت بلا راع وأسديت الشيء أي أهملته وأسديت حاجتي صيعتها ولم أعتن بها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r3.speaker: شاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r3.claim: An unnamed poet swears that God created nothing in vain, illustrating the word suda.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر فأقسم بالله جهد اليمين ما خلق الله شيئا سدى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r4.claim: Suda is an accusative circumstantial complement of the pronoun in yutraka; the verb phrase occupies the two-object position, and the question is a repudiating one.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r4.anchor: ونصب سدى على الحال من ضمير يترك وإن يترك في موضع المفعولين ليحسن والاستفهام إنكاري

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r5.claim: Repeating the question about humanity reiterates the denial of resurrection; moral wisdom requires commands and prohibitions, while accountability needs recompense that may not occur in this life.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r5.anchor: لتكرير إنكار الحشر قيل مع تضمن الكلام الدلالة على وقوعه حيث أن الحكمة تقتضي الأمر بالمحاسن والنهي عن القبائح والرذائل والتكليف لا يتحقق إلا بمجازاة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r6.claim: Some treat the argument from moral accountability as a rational proof of resurrection, but al-Ālūsī says this reasoning is debatable.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#3/r6.anchor: وجعل بعضهم هذا استدلالا عقليا على وقوع الحشر وفيه بحث لا يخفى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r4.claim: Faith in God, angels, scriptures, messengers, and the Last Day, followed by prayer and good works, yields fearful obedience and repeated glad tidings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r4.anchor: بأن صدق بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر وأقبل وأقام الصلاة فتبعتها جميع الأعمال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r5.claim: The denier acts as though he has no master or obligations and may follow his desires without command, prohibition, or accountability.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r5.anchor: فكان ظانا أنه مهمل لا مالك له وأنه هو السيد لا عبودية عليه , فلا يؤمر ولا ينهى ولا يعمل إلا بمقتضى شهواته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r6.claim: The question rebukes the assumption of being left unattended and exposes it as a product of deficient reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r6.anchor: قال منكرا ليه معبرا بالحسبان الذي الحامل عليه نقص العقل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r7.claim: The human is a created servant, weak, incapable, and needy, as his own condition and that of his kind show.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r7.anchor: أي الذي هو عبد مربوب ضعيف عاجز محتاج بما يرى في نفسه وأبناء جنسه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r8.claim: The passive wording stresses abandonment without specifying an abandoner: the imagined problem is being left wholly without purpose or care.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r8.anchor: ولما كان الحامل على الجراءة مطلق الترك هملا , لا كون الترك من معين , قال بانيا للمفعول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r9.claim: Being left futile means having no obligation, reward, judgment before the Creator, or reckoning for gratitude for His gifts.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r9.anchor: أي مهملا لاعبا لاهيا لا يكلف ولا يجازى ولا يعرض على الملك الأعظم الذي خلقه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r10.claim: Divine wisdom requires commands, prohibitions, and recompense; since many oppressors and victims die unrewarded, resurrection for judgment must occur.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r10.anchor: فإنها تقتضي الأمر بالمحاسن والنهي عن المساوئ والجزاء على كل منهما , وأكثر الظالمين والمظلومين يموتون من غير جزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r11.claim: A wise maker would not create something only to waste it, so the Creator’s wise ordering rules out leaving people without purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r11.anchor: لا يجوز في عقل عاقل أن صانعا يصنع شيئا ويتركه ضياعا وهو حكيم أو حاكم

DURR-FULL:v8p363/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p363/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p363/r1.claim: Mujahid explains that a person is not left purposeless, without commands or prohibitions.
DURR-FULL:v8p363/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {أن يترك سدى} قال: باطلا لا يؤمر ولا ينهى

DURR-FULL:v8p363/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p363/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p363/r2.claim: Qatada glosses being left sudā as being neglected.
DURR-FULL:v8p363/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أن يترك سدى} قال: أن يهمل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses sudan as being left idle or neglected.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : سدى هملا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r1.claim: The context makes “left” mean left in nonexistence without revival, as in 75:3 and 75:13; the passive is concise because God’s agency is already clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r1.anchor: والمراد بما يترك عليه الإنسان هنا ما يدل عليه السياق ، أي حال العدم دون إحياء مما دل عليه قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r2.claim: The inserted word “sudā” signals that God’s purpose in creating people entails reviving them after death to recompense their deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r2.anchor: فجاء ذكر سدى } هنا على طريقة الإدماج فيما سيق له الكلام ، إيماء إلى أن مقتضى حكمة خلق الإنسان أن لا يتركه خالقه بعد الموت فلا يحييه ليجازيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.claim: Repeating the question reinforces the rebuke to deniers after the account of Judgment and its reckoning, like 23:115; it prepares for the material proof in 75:37.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.anchor: وفي إعادة { أيحسب الإنسان } تهيئة لما سيعقب من دليل إمكان البعث من جانب المادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r4.claim: Sudā means neglected or left unattended; ḍamma on the sīn is more common than fatḥa, the form serves for singular and plural, and its alif derives from wāw. Al-Kashshaf and al-Raghib do not explain it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r4.anchor: و { سدى } بضم السين وبالقصر : اسم بمعنى المهمل ويقال : سدى بفتح السين والضم أكثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r5.claim: Sudā is a circumstantial accusative describing the subject of the passive verb “is left.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r5.anchor: ووقع { سدى } في موضع الحال من ضمير { يترك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r6.claim: God’s carefully formed, rational human beings cannot be abandoned like animals: divine wisdom excludes equating the righteous with the corrupt, and divine power enables their final return.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r6.anchor: لا يليق بحكمته أن يهمله مثل الحيوان فيجعل الصالحين كالمفسدين والطائعين لربهم كالمجرمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r1.claim: The question in 75:3 argues that resurrection will occur; here the question about being left sudā argues from divine wisdom and accountability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r1.anchor: ولذلك قال في جانب الاستدلال على وقوع البعث { أيحسب الإنسان أن لن نجمع عظامه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r2.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r2.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says Quran scholars agreed, to his knowledge, that sudā describes someone who is neither commanded nor forbidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r2.anchor: وعن الشافعي : لم يختلف أهل العلم بالقرآن فيما علمت أن السدى الذي لا يؤمر ولا ينهى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r3.claim: Being left sudā is a metonym for receiving no recompense: worldly obligation to follow commands and prohibitions is intended to lead to repayment in the Hereafter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r3.anchor: وقد تبين من هذا أن قوله : { أن يترك سدى } كناية عن الجزاء لأن التكليف في الحياة الدنيا مقصود منه الجزاء في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.claim: The material argument explains leaving someone without revival; it does not separately elaborate leaving someone without recompense, since revival is for recompense. Sudā had already inserted the wisdom argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.anchor: وهذا البيان خاص بأحد معنيي الترك في الآية وهو تركه دون إحياء وأكتفي ببيان هذا عن بيان المعنى الآخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r1.claim: The person meant by al-insan here is Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r1.anchor: يعني أبا جهل أن يترك سدى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses suda as being left neglected without commands, prohibitions, or punishment; asdaytu an object means I neglected it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي يهمل فلا يؤمر ولا ينهى ولا يعاقب يقال أسديت الشيء أي أهملته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r3.claim: The following verse begins the argument for resurrection from the human being’s origin as a drop of semen.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#6/r3.anchor: ثم دل على البعث بقوله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#13/r1.claim: The disbeliever is not left neglected, without commands or prohibitions, resurrection, or recompense.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#13/r1.anchor: أيحسب الكافران يترك مهملا لا يؤمر ولا ينهى ولا يبعث ولا يجازي

BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet seized and shook Abū Jahl at al-Baṭḥāʾ, warned him, and Abū Jahl boasted of his invulnerability; at Badr he was felled by the sons of ʿAfrāʾ and finished by Ibn Masʿūd.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.anchor: وروى إنه لما نزلت هذه الآية أخذ رسول الله بمجامع ثوب أبي جهل بالبطحاء وهزه مرة أو مرتين

BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.claim: Aqaṣahu means to kill someone in place, while ajhaza means to finish off a wounded person who is near death.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.anchor: اقعصه قتله مكانه وأجهز على الجريح أثبت قتل وأسره وتمم عليه

BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.claim: The Prophet called every community a Pharaoh and identified Abū Jahl as this community’s Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.anchor: وكان رسول الله عليه السلام يقول إن لكل أمة فرعونا وإن فرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل

BURSEVI:v10p199/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r4.claim: The first reading is that a person will not be left alive without duties or recompense.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r4.anchor: أي يحيى حال كونه مهملا فلا يكلف ولا يجزي

BURSEVI:v10p199/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p199/r5.claim: Another reading is that a person will not be left in the grave without resurrection.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r5.anchor: وقيل أن يترك في قبره فلا يبعث سدى المهمل

BURSEVI:v10p199/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r6.claim: Suda means neglected or idle; the source also cites Arabic idioms for needs left uncompleted.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r6.anchor: سدى المهمل يقال أسدبت أبلى أسداء أي ملتها وتقول أسديت حاجتي وسديتها

BURSEVI:v10p199/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r7.claim: Repeating the denial rebuts the assumption of no resurrection: giving humans capacities and actions without duties would imply divine approval of evil, contrary to wisdom.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r7.anchor: وتكرير الإنكار لحسبانها يتضمن تكرير إنكاره للحشر

BURSEVI:v10p199/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r8.claim: Worldly obligations distinguish believers from corruptors; since this cramped world is not the place of full recompense, resurrection must follow so each is repaid for their deeds.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r8.anchor: ولا يجعل المتقين كالفجار ويجازي كل نفس بما تسعى

BURSEVI:v10p199/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r9.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v10p199/r9.claim: A great Sufi says it is bad adab to demand the immediate results of one’s deeds and spiritual states in this world, whose nature does not promise them.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r9.anchor: وقد قال بعض الكبار من طلب تعجيل نتائج أعماله وأحواله في هذه الدار فقد أساء الأدب

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r1.claim: Suda means left without instruction, prohibition, duty, or accountability for one's deeds in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r1.anchor: أي مهملا لا يؤمر ، ولا ينهى ، ولا يكلف في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r2.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r2.claim: Al-Suddi defines the word as neglected or left unattended, as when one lets camels loose.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r2.anchor: والسدي في اللغة المهمل يقال : أسديت إبلي إسداء أهملتها

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r3.claim: The verse returns to the opening question about whether God will gather human bones and supplies the first proof of resurrection: humans cannot have been given faculties without duties.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r3.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر في أول السورة ، قوله : { أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه }

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r4.claim: If God gave power, instruments, and reason without commands to obey or prohibitions against evil, that would imply approval of vile acts, contrary to divine wisdom; therefore there must be moral duty.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r4.anchor: وتقريره أن إعطاء القدرة والآلة والعقل بدون التكليف والأمر بالطاعة والنهي عن المفاسد يقتضي كونه تعالى راضيا بقبائح الأفعال ، وذلك لا يليق بحكمته

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r5.claim: Duty befits the gracious and merciful God only if there is an afterlife of reward and resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r5.anchor: فإذا لا بد من التكليف والتكليف لا يحسن ولا يليق بالكريم الرحيم إلا إذا كان هناك دار الثواب والبعث والقيامة

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r6.claim: Other verses likewise connect the coming Hour and moral accountability, and distinguish believers from wrongdoers and the pious from sinners.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#3/r6.anchor: ونظيره قوله : { إن الساعة ءاتية أكاد أخفيها لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى } ( طه : 15 )

STUDYQURAN:75:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:36/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:75:36/r1.claim: JJ takes aimless to mean being left without revealed religious obligations or accountability.
STUDYQURAN:75:36/r1.anchor: without being obligated to follow a revealed religion and without being held accountable?” (JJ).

STUDYQURAN:75:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:36/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:75:36/r2.claim: IK also understands aimless as neglected, referring to people who doubt that they will be resurrected.
STUDYQURAN:75:36/r2.anchor: Left aimless could also be understood to mean“neglected,” in which case it refers to those who doubt they will be resurrected (IK).

TAB-FULL:v23p526/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r1.claim: The disbelieving human is not left neglected without commands, prohibitions, or worship duties.
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى}

TAB-FULL:v23p526/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى}

TAB-FULL:v23p526/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains that the human is not left without commands and prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى}

TAB-FULL:v23p526/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd defines sudan as having no imposed duty and doing no work.
TAB-FULL:v23p526/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى}

TABATABAI:75:36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36/r6.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:75:36/r6.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi explains being left suda as being neither judged, punished, nor questioned about anything.
TABATABAI:75:36/r6.anchor: قال لا يحاسب ولا يعذب ولا يسأل عن شيء

TABATABAI:75:36/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36/r7.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام
TABATABAI:75:36/r7.claim: In a report through Musʿada ibn Ziyad, a man says humans were created for extinction; Jaʿfar al-Sadiq replies that they were created for permanence, since Paradise does not perish and Hell does not go out, and people move from one abode to another.
TABATABAI:75:36/r7.anchor: لجعفر بن محمد عليه السلام، يا أبا عبد الله

TABRISI:75:26-28/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:26-28/r11.claim: Sudā means neglected or left without purpose.
TABRISI:75:26-28/r11.anchor: والسدى المهمل والعلقة القطعة من الدم المنعقد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#5/r1.claim: Sudā means left neglected: neither commanded nor prohibited nor punished; asdaytu al-shayʾ means I left it neglected.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#5/r1.anchor: {أن يترك سدى} أي يهمل: فلا يؤمر، ولا ينهى، ولا يعاقب (4) . يقال: أسديت الشيء؛ إذا أهملته.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r5.speaker: جماعة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r5.claim: The commentators identify the human in this passage as Abu Jahl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: {أيحسب الإنسان} (¬1) قالوا (¬2): يعني أبا جهل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r6.claim: Sudā means left idle or neglected, without commands, prohibitions, admonition, or reckoning; asdaytu means leaving camels unattended.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r6.anchor: هملا، مهملا، لا يؤمر، ولا ينهى، ولا يوعظ في الدنيا, ولا يحاسب بعمله في الآخرة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد عن أبي زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r7.claim: Abu ʿUbayd, citing Abu Zayd, gives the usage “I left my camels unattended” and sudā as the verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r7.anchor: يقال: أسديت إبلي إسداء أهملتها، والاسم: السدى .. ذكر ذلك (أبو عبيد) (¬4)، (عن أبي زيد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r8.claim: The best fit is that the human is left without resurrection, as the following argument about his origin shows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r8.anchor: والأشبه بالمعنى في {سدى}، أي: مهملا لا يبعث. يدل عليه قوله في الدلالة على البعث

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r1.claim: The rebuking question asks whether a person imagines being left neglected, without resurrection after death.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r1.anchor: أيظن الانسان أن يترك مهملا لا يعتنى به فلا يبعث بإحيائه بعد الموت

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r2.claim: Suda means neglected or left unattended; such abandonment would entail no obligation and no recompense.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r2.anchor: والسدى المهمل، والمعنى أيظن الانسان أن يترك مهملا

TABRISI:75:29-36/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r19.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:75:29-36/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify the human as Abū Jahl and take suda as being left without command or prohibition.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r19.anchor: { أيحسب الإنسان } يعني أبا جهل { أن يترك سدى } مهملا لا يؤمر ولا ينهى عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:75:37-40/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:37-40/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:37-40/r1.claim: Alternatively, it is a general rebuke to an unbeliever who denies resurrection and thinks he will be abandoned without duties that reform and benefit him in this life and the next.
TABRISI:75:37-40/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنه عام أي أيظن الإنسان الكافر بالبعث الجاحد لنعم الله أن يترك مهملا من غير أمر يؤخذ به

THALABI:v10p92/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p92/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p92/r1.claim: Suda means left idle, with no commands or prohibitions; Arabic usage also describes a neglected need or unattended grazing camels.
THALABI:v10p92/r1.anchor: أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى هملا لا يؤمر ولا ينهى يقال: أسديت حاجتي أي ضيعتها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r6.claim: A person is not left neglected, without commands or prohibitions.

ELMALILI:75:36-40/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:36-40/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:36-40/r1.claim: Sudā means left unattended, without obligation, aimlessly, or abandoned to one’s own preference.
ELMALILI:75:36-40/r1.anchor: “Südâ” mühmel, teklifsiz, başıboş, kendi keyfine bırakılmış ilişiksiz demektir.

ITQAN:v2p335#5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p335#5/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p335#5/r4.claim: Sudan means left neglected or without purpose.

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r5.claim: To be left sudan means to be left without commands or prohibitions.
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r5.anchor: أي أن يترك غير مأمور وغير منهي

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r6.claim: Zajjāj moves from rejecting an aimless life to demonstrating Resurrection through God's power to initiate creation.

NASHR:v2p42/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p42/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
NASHR:v2p42/r6.claim: Reports from Abū Bakr differ on pausal imāla in سوى and سدى: both imāla and fatḥ are valid, though the Iraqi transmitters know only fatḥ.
NASHR:v2p42/r6.anchor: والوجهان جميعا عنه صحيحان، والفتح طريق العراقيين قاطبة لا يعرفون غيره

NASHR:v2p42/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p42/r7.speaker: المصريون والمغاربة
NASHR:v2p42/r7.claim: Egyptian and Maghrebi transmitters from Shuʿayb report imāla at pause for both words, along with those who use imāla elsewhere.
NASHR:v2p42/r7.anchor: روى المصريون، والمغاربة قاطبة عن شعيب عنه الإمالة في الوقف مع من أمال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r1.claim: Suda means left idle, without commands or prohibitions.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r2.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says it means neglected, like camels grazing wherever they please without a herder.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: معناه المهمل وإبل سدى إذا كانت ترعى حيث شاءت بلا راع.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r5.claim: Sudā means left without duties or requital.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r6.claim: The question renews the denial of resurrection and argues for it: wisdom requires commands to do good and avoid evil, which entails requital; since this may not occur in this life, it must occur in the next.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r6.anchor: وهو يتضمن تكرير إنكاره للحشر والدلالة عليه

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses suda as left neglected or at loose ends.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {أن يترك سدى} قال: هملا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r6.claim: The passage resumes its opening argument for resurrection: a person who expects no gathering of his bones may also imagine that he will be left in nonexistence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r6.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي عاد به الكلام إلى الاستدلال على إمكان البعث وهو ما ابتدىء به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r7.claim: Divine wisdom entails that a human will not be abandoned without purpose or care.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r7.anchor: وزيد هنا أن مقتضى الحكمة الإلاهية إيقاعه بقوله : { أن يترك سدى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r8.claim: The question is a denial, matching the earlier denial-form question about whether God will gather human bones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r8.anchor: والاستفهام إنكاري مثل الذي سبقه في قوله تعالى : { أيحسب الإنسان أن لن نجمع عظامه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r9.claim: Leaving originally means voluntarily parting from something; metaphorically it means neglecting someone without care or attention, which is the sense here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r9.anchor: وأصل معنى الترك : مفارقة شيء شيئا اختيارا من التارك ، ويطلق مجازا على إهمال أحد شيئا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters say the entire passage concerns Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.anchor: قال جمهور المتأولين: هذه الآية كلها إنما نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r12.claim: أيحسب is rebuke and سدى means left without commands or prohibitions; reflection on human beginnings establishes that resurrection is possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r12.anchor: وقوله تعالى: أيحسب توقيف وتوبيخ، وسدى معناه مهملا لا يؤمر ولا ينهى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi explains being left without purpose as being left without resurrection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد والشافعي وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r2.claim: Mujahid, al-Shafi'i, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam explain it as being left without commands or prohibitions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد، والشافعي، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: يعني لا يؤمر ولا ينهى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says the verse includes both meanings: people are not neglected in worldly life without commands, nor left in the grave without resurrection; it establishes the afterlife against its deniers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الآية تعم الحالين، أي: ليس يترك في هذه الدنيا مهملا لا يؤمر ولا ينهى، ولا يترك في قبره سدى لا يبعث

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r4.claim: Sudā means left unattended without being held accountable; the related expression for camels means grazing wherever they please.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r4.anchor: السدى: المهمل، وهو أن يهمل من غير أن يؤخذ به

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r9.claim: This verse explains that people are not left without purpose or accountability; its initial hamzah is an interrogative used here to deny and rebuke the thought.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r9.anchor: ثم بين تعالى أنهم لم يتركوا هملا زجرا لهم

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r10.claim: The initial alif is an interrogative, with the force of disapproval.

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r11.claim: Al-insān means humankind generally, which the author says is the stronger view; Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify the referent as Abū Jahl.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r11.anchor: الإنسان، قيل: أراد الجنس وهو الوجه. وقيل: أراد أبا جهل

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r12.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid take the claim of being left suda as being left neglected, with no commands or prohibitions.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r12.anchor: أن يترك سدى مهملا، لا يؤمر ولا ينهى، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r3.claim: One view asks whether a person thinks no deed will be required of him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r3.anchor: فهل لا يفترض عليه عمل , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r4.claim: Another view is that a person thinks he will not be resurrected.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r5.claim: A third view takes sada as being left without commands or prohibitions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r5.anchor: ملغى لا يؤمر ولا ينهى , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r6.claim: A fourth view is that a person is left without reckoning or punishment; the cited poet says God leaves nothing neglected.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r6.anchor: عبث لا يحاسب ولا يعاقب , قال الشاعر : فأقسم بالله جهد اليمين

MUQATIL:75:34-40/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r3.claim: The human being is not left neglected without being held to account for his deeds; Muqatil applies it to Abu Jahl through the end of the sura.
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r3.anchor: { أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى } [آية: 36] يعني مهملا لا يحاسب بعمله، يعني أبا جهل إلى آخر السورة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd and Mujahid say the son of Adam is not left neglected without commands or prohibitions; camels left grazing without a herder illustrate sudā.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r1.anchor: أي أن يخلى مهملا، فلا يؤمر ولا ينهى قاله ابن زيد ومجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r2.claim: Another view asks whether a person is left in the grave forever without resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r2.anchor: وقيل: أيحسب أن يترك في قبره كذلك أبدا لا يبعث

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r3.claim: A poem says God left nothing neglected, illustrating sudā.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر: فأقسم بالله جهد اليمين ما ترك الله شيئا سدى
